title: Acromioclavicular joint (AC joint) and lateral clavicle injuries – clinical and imaging-based analyses.
summary:
This project investigates injuries of the acromioclavicular (AC) joint, focusing in particular on ligament damage. We aim to identify which factors are associated with better functional recovery.
The goal is to determine factors that allow for optimal treatment and a faster return to normal shoulder movement. Patients will be treated according to current guidelines, either conservatively (without surgery) or surgically. They will then be followed up at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months, and 24 months – with clinical assessments, imaging when indicated, and questionnaires addressing pain, function, and satisfaction.
Associated injuries, for example in the joint space or the adjacent shoulder joint, will be identified at the start using MRI. We are testing the hypothesis that patients with seemingly minor injuries who continue to experience pain often have additional associated injuries. Furthermore, we propose that minor AC joint injuries can usually be managed without surgery, although some complaints may persist in the long term.
conditions: Fracture of the clavicle: medial third

interventions.name: Prospective bicentric study on acromioclavicular joint injuries – UKSH Campus Kiel in cooperation with the Lubinus Clinic Kiel.”

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ACJ-Dislocation
Fraktures of the lateral Clavicle
Exclusion criteria:
Adjacent fracture of the shoulder joint, previous surgery on the AC joint, contraindication to MRI (e.g., pregnancy, claustrophobia, metal implants, etc.)
